Unofficial connector, not affiliated with Roon Labs. It talks to your **Roon
Core** (Roon Server, Nucleus, ROCK, or the Roon app acting as Core) on the
local network, through the official Roon extension API: no account, no cloud.

> Built from the Roon API documentation: it was **never tested with a real Roon Core**.
> Reports are welcome (GitHub issues of `LM1LC3N7/gladys-roon`).

Requires Gladys 5.3.0 or later (the Music widget).

## What you get

One Gladys device per **Roon output** (a room, a speaker, a DAC), with:

- playback: play, pause, stop (the Music widget), previous, next;
- the track playing: title, artist, album, artwork, duration and position;
- shuffle and repeat (off, all, one);
- volume (0-100 % of the range of the output) and mute, when Roon can set
  the volume of the output (not for a fixed volume nor for +/- only
  controls);
- the name of the zone the output plays in (e.g. "Living room + Kitchen"
  when grouped).

Two scene actions: **group two outputs** (the zone keeps the queue of the
first one) and **take an output out of its group**.

## Setup

1. Type the **address** of the Roon Core (give it a fixed address in your
   router), or click **Find the Roon Core**: Gladys asks the local network,
   and when exactly one Core answers and no address is typed, its address is
   saved. The **port** is 9330 for Roon 2 (9100 for older versions).
2. In Roon, open **Settings > Extensions** and click **Enable** next to
   **Gladys (community)** (publisher LM1LC3N7, a community integration, not
   made by the Gladys Assistant team). Until then the status says it is waiting for the
   authorization.
3. Open the **Discovery** tab and add the outputs you want.

The authorization the Core gives is kept in the `/data` folder of the
integration (never in the logs, never shown). **Forget the Roon
authorization** deletes it: the extension then has to be enabled again in
Roon.

## Volume cap

**Volume cap (%)**, 50 by default: the highest volume Gladys may set, in
percent of the range of each output (100: no cap). A higher volume asked by a
scene or the dashboard is set to the cap, rounded down to a step of the
output, and never above the limits set in Roon. Unmuting first brings the
volume back under the cap when it is above (and is refused when the volume of
the output is unknown, while a cap applies). The volume changed in Roon itself
is not touched.

## Commands and their answers

A command is a success when the Core accepted it **and** the state Roon sends
back shows it (play, pause, stop, volume, mute, shuffle, repeat, grouping).
Seek, previous and next succeed when the Core accepts them. A command whose
state is already there (play on a zone playing) succeeds at once; a volume the
Core trims (a limit set in Roon) answers "not yet seen applied" although it
is done. Otherwise the
answer says what happened: "nothing sent", "sent, without an answer (not
confirmed)", "accepted, not yet seen applied (not confirmed)" or "refused by
the Roon Core".

**Pause, stop, mute and a lower volume are not held by the volume cap.** They
are refused only when nothing can receive them:

- the Roon Core is not connected (or not yet authorized);
- the output is not in Roon right now (off, renamed or removed);
- the value is invalid;
- for mute and volume: the output has no volume Gladys can set;
- more than 256 requests are already waiting for the Core (a Core that stopped
  answering; other commands are held from 64 on).

When two outputs or more have the name of the device, pause, stop, mute and a
lower volume go to every one of them (a volume only to those it lowers); play,
unmute, a higher volume and the other commands are refused (which room would
it be?). A zone that cannot pause (a live radio) is stopped instead. An unmute that
waits for its volume step is not sent when another command for the same
output was clicked meanwhile (a mute clicked after it is never overtaken).

## Good to know

- **Identity**: an output is identified by its name in Roon, as Home Assistant
  does (Roon may change its internal ids). Renaming an output in Roon gives a
  new device in Gladys and leaves the old one "unreachable": the scenes using
  it stop working, without an error. **Swapped names** (two outputs trading
  their names in Roon) are seen from the output ids last seen for each name
  (kept in `/data`): the volume never goes to the other room; until you open
  Discovery again (which takes the new names), the device publishes nothing
  (its badge shows "unreachable"),
  pause, stop, mute and a lower volume go to the room it was made for, and
  the other commands are refused. Two outputs with the same name are left out of Discovery and
  publish nothing.
- **Network**: the Roon extension API is plain `ws://` on the local network:
  the authorization token and the commands travel in clear text on it, like for
  every Roon extension. The token is sent to whatever answers at the address
  typed with the id of the Core it came from.
- The states come live from the Core (subscription), nothing is polled. After
  a loss of the Core, nothing is published until the Core is back; the badge
  of the devices shows "unreachable" meanwhile. The connection is tried again
  after 5 s, then 10 s, up to every 2 minutes.
- The artwork is fetched from the Core (400 px, at most 300 KB) when Gladys
  shows it.
- No playlists, library or radio browsing yet (see the TODO of the
  repository).

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Roon zones (unofficial) asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Roon in Gladys | `section` | No | Unofficial connector, not affiliated with Roon Labs. It talks to your Roon Core on the local network through the official Roon extension API (no account, no cloud): one Gladys device per Roon output, with play, pause, stop, previous, next, volume, mute, shuffle, repeat, the track playing and its artwork for the Music widget, and grouping by scene actions. Type the address of the Core (or click "Find the Roon Core"), then in Roon open Settings > Extensions and click Enable next to "Gladys (community)". Then open Discovery to add the outputs. |
| Roon Core address | `string` | No | IP address (or host name) of the computer or appliance running the Roon Core (Roon Server, Nucleus, ROCK…). Give it a fixed address in your router. "Find the Roon Core" fills it in when one Core answers. |
| Roon Core port | `number` | No | The port of the extension API: 9330 for Roon 2, 9100 for older versions. |
| Volume cap (%) | `number` | No | The highest volume Gladys may set, in percent of the range of each output, from 1 to 100 (100: no cap). A higher volume asked by a scene or the dashboard is set to this cap; unmuting brings the volume back under the cap first. The volume set in Roon itself is not changed, and a lower volume, pause, stop and mute are never held by the cap. |

## How to install Roon zones (unofficial) in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Roon zones (unofficial) appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-roon:0.1.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-roon](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-roon).

Roon zones (unofficial) requires Gladys `>=5.3.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Roon zones (unofficial) is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), not by the Gladys core team.
